title: Xbox, GTA 6 için özel bulut yayın hakları alındığı iddialarını yalanladı
summary: Xbox, Grand Theft Auto 6 için özel bulut yayın hakları aldığına yönelik haberlerin ardından iddiaları yalanladı.
body:
VGC ve Eurogamer'ın aktardığına göre Xbox, Grand Theft Auto 6 için özel bulut yayın hakları elde ettiği yönündeki iddiaları yalanladı. Süreç, Xbox CEO'su Asha Sharma'nın çalışanlarla yaptığı bir toplantıda şirketin oyun hakkında farklı planları olduğunu belirtmesiyle gündeme gelmişti. The Verge'ün bu toplantıya dayandırdığı haberi, Xbox'ın oyunu Xbox Cloud Gaming üzerinden özel olarak yayınlayacağını ve bu sayede PC gibi platformlara da taşıyacağını öne sürmüştü.

## İddialara resmi yalanlama geldi

Haberlerin ardından Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball, X platformu üzerinden yaptığı açıklamada oyunun Xbox'ta özel olarak akış yapılmayacağını ve PC'ye bu yolla gelmeyeceğini duyurdu. Ball, oyunun Xbox konsolları için 19 Kasım'da piyasaya çıkmasını dört gözle beklediklerini belirtti. Konuşulan iddiaların aksine, şirket yetkilileri konsollara özel bulut yayın hakları konusunda kesin bir detay paylaşmazken, Rockstar Games cephesinden henüz resmi bir akış anlaşması duyurulmadı.

## Xbox tarafında büyüme mesajı

Öte yandan Xbox CEO'su Asha Sharma, şirketin ilk taraf oyun sektöründe yeniden büyüme eğilimine girdiğini açıkladı. Sharma, Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2 ve World of Warcraft Forever yapımlarının güçlü bir başlangıç yaptığını, markaya yönelik olumlu algının da son bir yılda arttığını ifade etti.

**Neden önemli?** Yapılan resmi yalanlama, GTA 6'nın bulut üzerinden farklı platformlara geleceği yönündeki beklentileri netleştirirken, oyunun çıkış tarihi yaklaşırken platform stratejilerinin şekillendiğini gösteriyor.

source_texts.title: Xbox has ‘started to return to growth’ in first-party following an ‘all-time low’, CEO Asha Sharma reportedly tells staff
source_texts.summary: The previous strategy was leading to "freefall" financial declines… Source
source_texts.text:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has reportedly told staff that the company has “started to return to growth” in its first-party games sector.
Sharma held an internal town hall with Xbox employees on Tuesday, and Windows Central reports that she updated staff on the status of the company’s ongoing ‘reset’, which has already seen numerous layoffs and the closure, release or restructuring of a number of studios.
According to the report, Sharma told staff that Xbox was declining in hours spent, players and revenue at the start of the year, but has now stabilised in terms of hours spent.
She also stated that after declines year-over-year in the first-party games sector, the company has now returned back to growth in this area, telling staff that it was now “more than two to three times what we were”, though what this entails in actual numbers doesn’t appear to have been confirmed.
“We’re making the right decisions to reinvest in the business,” she reportedly said, “after an all time low, we’ve started to return to growth, more than two to three times what we were, and we expect that continue”.
Sharma is said to have cited Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2 and World of Warcraft Forever, saying they had “strong” starts, and claimed that Xbox had seen a 30% increase in positive brand sentiments in the past year.
The report says Sharma also told staff that the previous Game Pass strategy had sent Xbox into “freefall” declines, but also suggested that Game Pass may get more “flexible for more players” in the future.
“Why do we exist?” Sharma reportedly said to staff. “We exist to be where the world plays, we will know when we have a billion daily active people, and we have a right to win because we’re now focused on our fans and franchises.”
In July, Microsoft enacted sweeping layoffs across the Xbox business as part of a widespread ‘reset’, initially affecting 1,600 jobs. Last month Xbox enacted the second wave of these planned cuts, leading to a further 268 layoffs.
It also announced that Rare, World’s Edge and the Halo franchise were moving to Activision, that Obsidian Entertainment was being rolled into Bethesda, and that Forza Motorsport studio Turn 10 and Forza Horizon studio Playground Games were merging, while Ninja Theory was likely to close.

source_texts.text:
Xbox has denied reports suggesting it obtained exclusive game-streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto 6 . The initial suggestion came from a report on The Verge , which cited an all-hands meeting in which CEO Asha Sharma allegedly told staff that Xbox plans to do something "no other platform holder is doing" around GTA 6.

The report inferred that Xbox had acquired exclusive game streaming rights for GTA 6, which would allow anyone using Xbox's Cloud Gaming service to stream GTA 6 on any supported platform - including on PC where the game won't natively be available.

Shortly after the report was published, however, Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball took to X to quash the suggestion and said Xbox won't be streaming GTA 6 exclusively , nor will the game be available that way on PC. "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see," Ball said, "it has also led to some misreporting. We are looking forward to launching GTA 6 on Xbox November 19, though the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC."

Nevertheless, Ball didn't deny Xbox having cloud streaming rights for GTA 6 on Xbox consoles specifically, which could be what the deal is actually about . If it is, an Xbox user would need to purchase a copy of GTA 6 and subscribe to Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream the game to - seemingly - anything but a PC.

Xbox's cloud streaming service has changed dramatically in recent months. Following Sharma's appointment as CEO, the company has capped the number of Cloud Gaming play-hours available to Game Pass members . After years of no limits, Game Pass users are now limited to just 15 hours per month at the highest tier, Ultimate, which is reportedly a tipping-point where the streaming service stops being profitable for Microsoft .

In November, perhaps timed around the launch of GTA 6, Xbox is also launching Xbox Cloud Gaming as a standalone service that anyone can use without the need for a Game Pass membership. This paid model allows users to buy chunks of playtime hours to stream games they own to supported devices.

Xbox is also exploring different business models around game streaming. The company is already testing an ad-supported, free tier of Cloud Gaming with Xbox Insiders , and a November launch for that tier would make sense.

Beyond the Xbox portion of the report, Rockstar has not announced any GTA 6 streaming deals with any provider, though that could change as we get closer to the game's 19th November release date.
